learning_extracted: V3-EXQ-925's committed_fraction=0.000 was a driver instrumentation defect, not a substrate regime: one added post_action_update call per step (the standard update_residue path, ~14 direct callers / ~382 call references across the driver corpus) takes committed_fraction from 0.000 to 1.000 at unchanged default config. Red-team verified at the 925-ERA commit 9bcde4cb (not just today's tree): both GSCT call sites sat inside `elif committed:` then too, so the 925 autopsy's recommended lever was incapable of producing the regime it was recommended to produce, and its 'mechanically why commitment never engaged' attribution was wrong against the substrate as it stood at run time. Precision on the evidence: the cross-run 0.000 -> 1.000 spans two substrate commits and machines; the CONTROLLED demonstration is the authoring-time probe (same substrate, one added call, 0.000 -> 0.959).

The scientifically load-bearing residue, CORRECTED at the 7c red-team pass: what persists in the committed regime is SCORE FLATNESS, not near-uniform SELECTION. ARM_COMMIT's selection was exactly deterministic (c0_argmin_matches_factual_rate = 1.0); the entropy-0.9988 softmax is an explicitly-labelled diagnostic distribution (last_precommit_probs) that generated no behaviour, so the manifest's own 'NO channel is meaningfully steering the choice' prose absolute is refuted by the run's own deterministic-selector columns: the F-lesion flips the ACTUAL committed winner on 9.7% (ARM_COMMIT) / 19.2% (GSCT) of events, and the F-scramble on 19.2% / 30.4%. What makes the run uninformative for H1-H4 is that those winner-flips are chance-DIRECTIONAL (c1_frac_moved_toward_safer 0.530 / 0.484): F has real argmin-level authority over near-flat scores, exercised with no consistent alignment to the safety axis. The fair-test blocker for H1-H4 is absolute score SCALE/flatness (registry leg H5, confirmed from V3-EXQ-936), not commitment -- but the evidence shape is directionless winner-flips, not 'tiny deltas'. The manifest inherited the conflation (its note builder is regime-unconditioned and the driver carries a stale 'selector is running UNCOMMITTED' comment; its failure_localisation also points at a SELECTOR REGIME note this run suppresses) -- driver hygiene items for any successor.
925a cannot contrast committed vs uncommitted within-run (committed_fraction 1.000 everywhere, zero uncommitted events); 925 + 925a jointly cover the two regimes, as the queue note anticipated.

Seed 43's competitor channel carries ~7e-9 per-candidate signal in both arms across both runs -- a persistent per-seed training-reliability gap in gated_policy that bounds single-seed competitor-influence readings.
